segments.text: Lesson 31
segments.translation: 第31课

segments.text: The sculptor speaks
segments.translation: 雕塑家说话

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: What do you have to be able to do to appreciate sculpture?
segments.translation: 欣赏雕塑需要具备哪些能力？

segments.text: Appreciation of sculpture depends upon the ability to respond to form in 3 dimensions.
segments.translation: 对雕塑的欣赏取决于对三维形式做出反应的能力。

segments.text: That is perhaps why sculpture has been described as the most difficult of all arts;
segments.translation: 这也许就是为什么雕塑被称为所有艺术中最难的一门。

segments.text: certainly it is more difficult than the arts which involve appreciation of flat forms, shape in only two dimensions.
segments.translation: 当然，它比涉及平面形式、仅二维形状的艺术的欣赏更困难。

segments.text: Many more people are 'form-blind' than colour-blind.
segments.translation: “色盲”的人比“色盲”的人多得多。

segments.text: The child learning to see, first distinguishes only two-dimensional shape; it cannot judge distances, depths.
segments.translation: 孩子在学习看东西时，首先只能区分二维形状；

segments.text: Later, for its personal safety and practical needs, it has to develop (partly by means of touch) the ability to judge roughly 3-dimensonal distances.
segments.translation: 后来，出于人身安全和实际需要，它必须发展（部分通过触摸）判断大致3维距离的能力。

segments.text: But having satisfied the requirements of practical necessity, most people go no further.
segments.translation: 但在满足了现实需要后，大多数人就不再继续了。

segments.text: Though they may attain considerable accuracy in the perception of flat form,
segments.translation: 尽管他们在感知平面形状方面可能获得相当高的准确性，

segments.text: they do not make the further intellectual and emotional effort needed to comprehend form in its full spatial existence.
segments.translation: 他们没有付出进一步的智力和情感努力来理解形式的完整空间存在。

segments.text: This is what the sculptor must do.
segments.translation: 这是雕塑家必须做的。

segments.text: He must strive continually to think of and use, form in its full spatial completeness.
segments.translation: 他必须不断努力思考和使用形式的完整空间完整性。

segments.text: He gets the solid shape as it were, inside his head--he thinks of it, whatever its size, as if he were holding it completely enclosed in the hollow of his hand.
segments.translation: 他在他的脑袋里得到了原来的实体形状——他想到了它，无论它有多大，就好像他把它完全封闭在他的手掌中一样。

segments.text: He mentally visualizes a complex form from all round itself;
segments.translation: 他在脑海中想象出一个来自四周的复杂形状；

segments.text: he knows while he looks at one side what the other side is like; he identifies himself with its centre of gravity, its mass, its weight;
segments.translation: 当他看一侧时，他知道另一侧是什么样子；

segments.text: he realizes its volume as the space that the shape displaces in the air.
segments.translation: 他意识到它的体积是形状在空气中所取代的空间。

segments.text: And the sensitive observer of sculpture must also learn to feel shape simply as shape, not as description or reminiscence.
segments.translation: 敏感的雕塑观察者也必须学会将形状仅仅作为形状来感受，而不是作为描述或回忆。

segments.text: He must, for example, perceive an egg as a simple single solid shape quite apart from its significance as food,
segments.translation: 例如，他必须将鸡蛋视为一个简单的单一固体形状，而与它作为食物的意义无关，

segments.text: or from the literary idea that it will become a bird.
segments.translation: 或者来自它会变成一只鸟的文学观念。

segments.text: And so with solids such as a shell, a nut, a plum, a pear, a tadpole, a mushroom,
segments.translation: 对于诸如贝壳、坚果、李子、梨、蝌蚪、蘑菇等固体，

segments.text: a mountain peak, a kidney, a carrot, a tree-trunk, a bird, a bud, a lark, a ladybird, a bulrush, a bone.
segments.translation: 一座山峰、一颗肾脏、一根胡萝卜、一根树干、一只鸟、一个花蕾、一只云雀、一只瓢虫、一根芦苇、一根骨头。

segments.text: From these he can go on to appreciate more complex forms or combinations of several forms.
segments.translation: 由此，他可以继续欣赏更复杂的形式或几种形式的组合。
